details.name: Bitter Christmas
details.title: Bitter Christmas
details.description: Pedro AlmodÃ³var returns with a masterstroke! In Competition at the Cannes Film Festival, Bitter Christmas delivered a Spanish opening weekend box office that surpassed those of The Room Next Door and Parallel Mothers. Even the deepest wells of inspiration run dry. Refusing to become a has-been, a writer-director turns the lives of those around him into material for his scripts, blending reality and fiction. Meanwhile, an advertising director grieving her motherâs death tries to numb her pain through work, only to be struck down by severe, panic-induced headaches. Forced to step back, she travels to a remote island with her friend, seeking respite in a relationship charged with intimate friction. Two intersecting storylines mirror each other: those seeking relief remain consumed by tension, while those with ambition are drained of energy. Through AlmodÃ³varâs singular aesthetic, characters elegantly trap themselves within the beautiful cages of human emotion.

details.name: Look Back
details.title: Look Back
details.description:
Confident fourth-grader Fujino draws a four-panel manga for her school's class newspaper and earns the admiration of her classmates.
One day, however, she comes across a manga by Kyomoto, a classmate who has stopped attending school, published in that same newspaper â and is completely floored by her overwhelming talent. From then on, driven by a single-minded desire to improve, Fujino keeps drawing, but she cannot close the gap between them, and eventually gives up drawing altogether.
On graduation day, Fujino visits Kyomoto's house to deliver her diploma, and discovers that Kyomoto has been a devoted fan of her manga all along.
Bound together by their shared passion for manga, the two begin drawing manga together. As Fujino and Kyomoto spend irreplaceable days together, an unexpected event happens that will change their lives forever.

After the Trojan War, Odysseus faces a dangerous voyage back to Ithaca, meeting creatures like the Cyclops Polyphemus, Sirens, and Calypso along the way.
Written and directed by Christopher Nolan, The Odyssey is an epic fantasy adventure shot entirely with IMAX film cameras. The film stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, Tom Holland as Telemachus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, Robert Pattinson as Antinous and Zendaya as Athena.

He serves up classic Chinese dishes: the DragonâRaisingâItsâHead feast, candied sweet potatoes and Kung Pao chicken. He partners with restaurant manager Ma Junsheng (Jiang Qiming): Xu Fu handles the cooking, while Ma Junsheng takes care of guests. Together, they turn the littleâknown Dragon Restaurant into a thriving spot.


War soon breaks out, and local conditions quickly turn dangerous. Different armed groups clash across the region. What will happen to Xu Fu? Can Dragon Restaurant survive amid the chaos of war?

details.name: Trial of Hein (GFF)
details.title: Trial of Hein (GFF)
details.description:
After fourteen years away, Hein returns to his remote North Sea island home, only to discover that the close knit community no longer recognises him. Even his childhood friend keeps his distance, and convinced he is an impostor, the villagers convene a court to determine his true identity. As his memories contradict every witness's account, suspicion curdles into open hostility, forcing Hein to confront what he has long refused to see. The debut feature of director Kai StÃ¤nicke, whose screenplay draws on his own coming out experience, probes how memory and identity are shaped and distorted.

 

2026    Teddy Jury Award, Berlinale

details.title: The Family Approach (GFF)
details.description:
Almost like family, but always temporary: in a house beside an idyllic lake, three youth workers do everything they can to create a home for the children in their residential care. Between parental love, bureaucracy, and youth welfare services, they cook, comfort, read bedtime stories â and fight an often overwhelmed system on the children's behalf. Shift after shift, they offer what these kids need most: safety and someone on their side. A film about the superpower of raising a child, and family in all its forms.

details.name: Prosecution (GFF)
details.title: Prosecution (GFF)
details.description:
Young German-Korean prosecutor Seyo Kim is determined to bring far-right extremists to justice in Germany. When she survives a racist attack on her own life, she defies her superiors and takes the perpetrators to court herself, uncovering a right-wing network with ties deep into the institutions meant to stop it. Director Faraz Shariat's second feature is grounded in years of meticulous research into Germany's legal system and its handling of far-right violence, a subject that feels urgent at the moment.

 

2026    Panorama Audience Award, C.I.C.A.E. Award, Heiner Carow Prize, Berlinale

Young German-Korean prosecutor Seyo Kim is determined to bring far-right extremists to justice in Germany. details.title: Swan Lake (Paris Opera Ballet 2026 - 2027)
details.description:
Broadway Cinemas is proud to exclusively present the Paris Opera Ballet's spectacular 2026-2027 season! Kicking this season off are two world-renowned ballet classics coming straight to the big screen: Romeo and Juliet and Swan Lake.

 

Prince Siegfried is urged by his parents to choose a bride, but by the shores of a lake he meets a mysterious swan maiden, Odette, enchanted by the sorcerer Rothbart. Only a sincere vow can save her. Captivated, he swears eternal love, until he meets Odile, the black swan...

 

A magical ballet set to Tchaikovsky's sparkling music, Swan Lake was first created in 1877 for the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, later restaged by Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov. Nearly a century later, Rudolf Nureyev brought his own interpretation to the Paris Opera in 1984.

details.description:
In the seedy underbelly of 18th-century Paris, money is king. Nothing is sacred â even love itself can be bought for the right price. A native of this hedonistic underworld, Manon is caught between twin desires when she falls in love with the student Des Grieux. Steadfast and devoted, he offers the possibility of an honourable life. Yet, the riches promised by the world of Parisian society remain tempting...


Manonâs inner turmoil and struggle for survival lie at the devastating heart of Kenneth MacMillanâs 1974 adaptation of AbbÃ© PrÃ©vostâs novel. In this signature work of The Royal Ballet, MacMillanâs nuanced understanding of human psychology makes for an unflinching look into the moral degradation of Manonâs Paris, while all its decadence and decay are brought to life through Jules Massenetâs score and Nicholas Georgiadisâs designs.

At the meantime, Yohji is suspected as the murderer of a police officer. Scared and confused, Yohji flees and goes to Mei Ling, who looks identical to the android, for a fraud passport. Knowing Mei Ling is his brother's future wife, Yohji decides to kill her to save his own life. Being pursued by the police and the android, Yohji runs away with Mei Ling and starts their adventure.

Peter Wrightâs production of this festive family favourite sparkles to the wondrous swell of Tchaikovskyâs orchestral score, alongside the glow and grandeur of Julia Trevelyan Omanâs period designs.

details.name: Seven Winter in Tehran (GFF)

details.description:
Tehran, July 2007: Reyhaneh Jabbari, 19, has a business meeting with a new client. When he tries to rape her, she stabs him in self-defense. Later that day, she is arrested for murder. Her trial results in a death penalty sentence. Thanks to personal and secretly recorded videos provided by Reyhaneh's family, their testimonies and the letters written by Reyhaneh in prison, the ï¬lm retraces the fate of a woman who becomes a symbol of resistance and women's rights even beyond the borders of Iran.

 

2023     Compass-Perspektive Award, Berlinale

details.description:
Bryan Cranston (Breaking Bad) and Marianne Jean-Baptiste (Hard Truths) feature in a five-star, triumphantly acclaimed new production of Arthur Millerâs classic play, from visionary director Ivo Van Hove (A View from the Bridge).


One family, the heart of the American dream. When wartime delivers profits for Joe, it comes at a price when his partner is charged with criminal manufacturing deals, and his eldest son goes missing in action. Will peacetime bring peace of mind, or will he be confronted by the consequence of his actions?


Filmed live from the West End, Paapa Essiedu (I May Destroy You), Tom Glynn-Carney (House of the Dragon), and Hayley Squires (I, Daniel Blake) also feature in this disturbingly prescient play.

details.name: Good Trip
details.title: Good Trip
details.description: Shan, an art assistant, juggles responsibilities on the film set and at the hospital, where she cares for her father, Kuen. During her time at the hospital, Shan is tasked by the crew to collect a big bowl from the prop-studio. At her father's request, they discreetly leave the hospital together, embarking on an unexpected journey from the studio to Macau, and subsequently to Okinawa, allowing Kueng to address his unfulfilled wishes. Following his peaceful passing, Shan inherits not only memories but also a lasting sense of courage, optimism, and imaginative spirit that sustains her throughout life.

details.description:
On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the NÃ©pstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. 


Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracksâ"Bohemian Rhapsody,â "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Freeâ and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the countryâs top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity.

 

Donât miss Queen Budapest on IMAX screen and exclusive at Broadway Cinemas only !

details.name: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (KINO)
details.title: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (KINO)
details.description:
San Francisco, at the turn of the millennium. Monika Treut turns her camera on a community of artists, scholars, and performers who live beyond the boundaries of conventional gender, blending technology, biochemistry, and sheer boldness to reshape their identities on their own terms.

 

Asked whether they are male or female, the gendernauts simply answer: yes.

 

Made at a time when transgender lives were rarely portrayed with dignity or nuance, Gendernauts remains a landmark of queer cinema, celebrating gender not as a fixed destination but as an open, joyful frontier.

details.title_lang: {"en":"The Einstein of Sex - The Life and Work of Dr. Magnus Hirschfeld (KINO)","zh_hk":"ç·æ¥µå (KINO)"}
details.description: Long before Kinsey, there was Magnus Hirschfeld: physician, sexologist, socialist, Jew, homosexual, and the man the tabloids dubbed "the Einstein of Sex." Rosa von Praunheim's affectionate biopic charts Hirschfeld's extraordinary crusade as he founded the world's first gay rights organisation in 1897, battled Paragraph 175, and opened Berlin's pioneering Institute for Sexual Science in 1920, a haven for queer and trans lives that flourished through the Weimar years until Nazi students torched its library in 1933. Friedel von Wangenheim plays the doctor with owlish warmth, flanked by his aristocratic great love Baron von Teschenberg, devoted young Karl Giese, and the institute's guardian angel, housekeeper Dorchen. Mixing period drama, newsreel and von Praunheim's trademark impish humour, it is both a monument to a man the Nazis nearly erased from history and a reminder of how quickly hard-won progress can burn.

details.title: Good Bye, Lenin! (KINO)
details.description: When Alex's mother, a devoted socialist activist, falls into a coma in October 1989, she misses the fall of the Berlin Wall entirely. Eight months later, she awakens, her heart too fragile for the truth. To keep her alive, Alex goes to extraordinary lengths to preserve the illusion of a world that no longer exists. A landmark of world cinema and one of the most cherished German films ever made, Good Bye, Lenin! endures as a timeless testament to love, memory, and identity. Tonight's screening is a heartfelt homage to its visionary director, the late Wolfgang Becker.

details.name: Ghosted (KINO)
details.title: Ghosted (KINO)
details.description:
An extraordinary love story between two worlds: Hamburg artist Sophie travels to Taiwan to come to terms with the sudden, unexplained death of her lover Ai-ling. In Taipei, a journalist latches onto her heels, seemingly obsessed with Ai-ling's fate. At the same time, the mysterious stranger does everything in her power to seduce Sophie.

 

Inspired by Taiwan's rapid social and technological development alongside ancient Chinese culture, Monika Treut weaves a narrative that drifts between past and present. At its core lie Chinese ghost myths, where traditionally oppressed women become erotic, daring beings who finally follow their own desires, and thus also find a way to take revenge.

details.title_lang: {"en":"It Is Not the Homosexual Who Is Perverse, But the Society in Which He Lives (KINO)","zh_hk":"éåä¹ç½ª (KINO)"}
details.description: Few films can claim to have started a revolution. Two years after West Germany decriminalised homosexuality, Rosa von Praunheim detonated this scabrous agit-prop fable on national television. Young, provincial Daniel arrives in Berlin and drifts through the gay subcultures of the era, from bourgeois coupledom to bar cliques to cruising grounds, while a merciless voice-over flays gay men for their assimilation, self-hatred and political apathy, demanding they come out and organise. The scandal was seismic: furious TV debates, walkouts, and the founding of dozens of activist groups. The modern German gay liberation movement traces its birth directly to this one film. Restored and as confrontational as ever, this is queer cinema as a molotov cocktail: crude, hectoring, frequently hilarious, and utterly foundational. Half a century on, its closing rallying cry âout of the toilets, into the streets!â still rings in the air.

details.name: Tough Love (KINO)
details.title: Tough Love (KINO)
details.description:
A karate champion looks back and finds his life reduced to bitterness and numbness. In childhood, he was repeatedly abused by his parents. As an adult, he became a pimp, earned large sums of money, and was eventually sent to prison. The only constant presence in his life has been his partnerâthe one person who supports him and gives him the courage to keep going. Caught in this vicious cycle, how will he confront himself, between who he was and who he is?

 

The film presents the life of Andreas Marquardt through an interweaving of interviews and dramatized reenactments, tracing a trajectory from fear and humiliation to contempt, hatred, and violence. Von Praunheim reconstructs the story through highly stylized scenes, capturing the interior design aesthetics of West Berlin at the time, and revealing the deep psychological trauma left by domestic abuse.

details.name: The Loneliest Man in Town (KINO)
details.title: The Loneliest Man in Town (KINO)
details.description:
Blues musician Al Cook lives surrounded by memories: his Viennese apartment crammed with vinyl records, videotapes, and a lifetime of devotion to a music he loves from an ocean away. When a ruthless real estate company targets his home for demolition, he must let go of his treasures one by one and face a radical new beginning.

 

From award-winning Austrian duo Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel, this quietly moving and unexpectedly funny portrait of loss and passion blurs the line between reality and fiction, bringing a real-life bluesman to the screen through non-professional performance and the warm, grainy textures of Super 16mm film. Premiered in competition at the Berlinale 2026.

 

Supported by Austrian Consulate General Hong Kong

details.name: Amrum  (KINO)
details.title: Amrum  (KINO)
details.description: On the remote island of Amrum in spring 1945, 12-year-old Nanning braves treacherous seas for seal hunting, fishes through the night, and tends the fields to keep his family alive. But as long-awaited peace finally arrives, unforeseen challenges compel him to chart his own course through the turbulent waters of post-war life. From one of Germany's leading directors, Fatih Akin, and inspired by the real childhood memories of acclaimed screenwriter Hark Bohm, AMRUM is a sweeping, deeply moving story of resilience and self-discovery. Premiered at Cannes 2025 and received 6 nominations at the German Film Awards.

details.name: Two Mountains Weighing Down My Chest (KINO)
details.title: Two Mountains Weighing Down My Chest (KINO)
details.description: Two starkly different cultural worlds, Berlin and Beijing, collide in this reflection on identity. Beijing born director Viv Li lands in post pandemic Berlin and immerses herself in the city's queer scene, an encounter that shakes her to the core and clashes with the traditional family values instilled back home, exposing how elusive self identity can be amid East West differences in a globalised world. This semi autobiographical documentary constantly asks "who am I", intercutting Berlin's dazzling nightlife, family dinners in Beijing and drunken heart to heart talks in New York, piecing together her own path through humour.

details.title: Genderation (KINO)
details.description: San Francisco, at the turn of the millennium. Monika Treut turns her camera on a community of artists, scholars, and performers who call themselves âGendernautsâ: they llive beyond the boundaries of conventional gender, blending technology, biochemistry, and sheer boldness to reshape their identities on their own terms. Made at a time when transgender lives were rarely portrayed with dignity or nuance, Gendernauts remains a landmark of queer cinema, celebrating gender not as a fixed destination but as an open, joyful frontier. Winner of the Teddy Award at the Berlinale.

Twelve people dream of a home while world history refuses to spare their small shore. Adapting Jenny Erpenbeck's novel, Palme d'Or winner Volker SchlÃ¶ndorff crafts a textured, compassionate epic with Lars Eidinger and Martina Gedeck that premiered in Cannes, a fitting late career triumph.

details.name: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Before the world had the vocabulary, San Francisco had the âgendernautsâ. At the giddy height of the late-90s tech boom, Monika Treut embedded herself among the Bay Area's community of trans and gender-fluid artists, activists and academics: historian Susan Stryker, "Goddess of Cyberspace" Sandy Stone, video artists Texas Tomboy and Jordy Jones, intersex activist Hida Viloria, and the irrepressible Annie Sprinkle. These voyagers were charting identities beyond the binary decades ahead of the culture, and Treut films them not as case studies but as pioneers: partying, working, skydiving, remaking their bodies and their world with wit and ferocious self-possession. Winner of the Teddy Award at the Berlinale, this landmark documentary now doubles as a time capsule of a freer, pre-gentrification San Francisco, and as proof that the future arrives first at the margins.

details.name: Ghosted (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Ghosted (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Grief has a way of following you across oceans. Hamburg artist Sophie Schmitt is undone by the sudden, unexplained death of her young Taiwanese lover, Ai-ling, and travels to Taipei with a video installation built in her memory. There she is pursued by Mei-li, a beguiling and persistent journalist who wants far more than an interview, and who soon materialises, unannounced, on Sophie's Hamburg doorstep. As seduction shades into investigation, past and present blur, and Monika Treut's cross-cultural mystery drifts elegantly toward the supernatural, steeped in Taiwanese ghost lore and the ache of unfinished love. The first German-Taiwanese co-production, shot between the night markets of Taipei and the grey light of Hamburg, GHOSTED premiered in the Berlinale's Panorama and remains one of Treut's most atmospheric works: a sapphic ghost story where the dead, like desire, refuse to stay buried.

details.title_lang: {"en":"It Is Not the Homosexual Who Is Perverse, But the Society in Which He Lives (HKLGFF 2026)","zh_hk":"éåä¹ç½ª (HKLGFF 2026)"}
details.description: Few films can claim to have started a revolution. Two years after West Germany decriminalised homosexuality, Rosa von Praunheim detonated this scabrous agit-prop fable on national television. Young, provincial Daniel arrives in Berlin and drifts through the gay subcultures of the era, from bourgeois coupledom to bar cliques to cruising grounds, while a merciless voice-over flays gay men for their assimilation, self-hatred and political apathy, demanding they come out and organise. The scandal was seismic: furious TV debates, walkouts, and the founding of dozens of activist groups. The modern German gay liberation movement traces its birth directly to this one film. Restored and as confrontational as ever, this is queer cinema as a molotov cocktail: crude, hectoring, frequently hilarious, and utterly foundational. Half a century on, its closing rallying cry (out of the toilets, into the streets!) still rings in the air.

details.name: Prosecution (KINO)
details.title: Prosecution (KINO)
details.description: Young German-Korean prosecutor Seyo Kim is determined to bring far-right extremists to justice in Germany. When she survives a racist attack on her own life, she defies her superiors and takes the perpetrators to court herself, uncovering a right-wing network with ties deep into the institutions meant to stop it. Director Faraz Shariat's second feature is grounded in years of meticulous research into Germany's legal system and its handling of far-right violence, a subject that feels urgent at the moment. With a commanding debut performance by Chen Emilie Yan in the lead role, the film premiered in the Panorama section of the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival, taking home three prizes.

details.name: Where To? (KINO)
details.title: Where To? (KINO)
details.description:
In the endless nights of Berlin, a 55 year old Palestinian Uber driver named Hassan shuttles revellers from one party to the next, estranged from his daughter and adrift without purpose. One night a young Israeli tourist exploring his sexuality far from home stumbles into his cab, and months later reappears, now living in Berlin and nursing a broken heart. Across two years of recurring rides, Hassan begins to recognise echoes of his own buried pain, and is finally pushed to confront the past that led him to leave his homeland thirty years ago. Perspectives programme at the 2026 Berlinale.

 

Supported by: Consulate General of Israel in Hong Kong and Macau

details.title: 25 Cats From Qatar (InDPanda)
details.description:
From the filmmaker of the award-winning CAT DADDIES (Opening Film of the 18th InDPanda). Qatar is one of the worldâs wealthiest nations, and its rapid growth is powered by migrant workers who make 89% of the population. But underneath the luxurious surface lies an overwhelming street cat population where disease is rampant, the heat is extreme, and expats are burdened to help the struggling felines.

 

When an American flight attendant and cat cafe owner becomes aware of the crisis, she hatches a plan to fly 25 cats to Milwaukee, where her cat cafe provides a pipeline for adoption.

 

This touching journey is both an urgent wake-up call and a compassionate and heartwarming portrayal of strangers overcoming international barriers to reach a common goal.

details.description: Martin Scorseseâs classic returns to cinemas for its 50th anniversary in a stunning 4K restoration. A Vietnam veteran back in New York, Travis Bickle works the graveyard shift as a taxi driver to cope with his chronic insomnia. Night after night, the cityâs moral decay and grimy streets disturb him as deeply as the horrors of the battlefield. Adrift and disillusioned, he becomes fixated on saving Iris, a teenage runaway drawn into prostitution, setting off on a violent path of no return. Robert De Niro and Jodie Foster deliver landmark performances, embodying a chilling descent into self-destruction. Winner of the Palme dâOr and nominated for four Academy Awards, Scorseseâs raw portrait of urban alienation remains an essential diagnosis of a society defined by loneliness. Half a century later, the meter is still running.

details.description: May 1980, A taxi driver named Man-seob in Seoul, comes across an offer too good to be true. If he drives a foreign passenger from Seoul down to Gwangju and back, heâll be paid the unthinkable sum money â enough to cover several months of unpaid rent. Without stopping to ask the details, he picks up the German reporter Peter and sets off along the highway. There they encounter students and ordinary citizens taking part in large-scale demonstrations against the government. Man-seob, alarmed by the danger in the air, pleads with Peter to go quickly back to Seoul. But Peter ignores him, and begins shooting with his news camera. As time passes the situation grows more and more serious, and Man-seob keeps thinking of his young daughter at home all alone.

details.title: Daddio (bcSunday)
details.description:
New York City. JFK airport. A young woman jumps into the backseat of a yellow taxi, the cabbie throwing the vehicle into drive as the two head out into the night toward Manhattan... and strike up the most unexpected conversation.

Daddio celebrates the power found in those rare moments of pure human connection, even with the most unlikely person. This highly contained, yet kinetic character-study -- encapsulated in one single cab ride -- explores the complexities inherent to the secrets we keep, particularly the ones locked away on our phones. Itâs about truth and illusion, how we so effortlessly substitute one for the other out of survival. Itâs about the hurtful memories of childhood, how past trauma can manifest itself in the most profound ways. Itâs about the beautiful dance between the pain and poetry that is the human experience.

Beneath the crushing weight of family, faith and community, their mutual attraction must be kept secret at all costs. But when tragedy strikes, their forbidden passion unleashes forces darker than either could imagine, and the villagers rally to drive out the evil they sense in their midst. Adapting Karl Heinrich Ulrichs's 1884 novella, director Kasper Kalle pours new blood into vampire lore with a haunting, subversive queer folk-horror that recalls Dreyer and Robert Eggers. Egor Venned and Pilou AsbÃ¦k smoulder against the stark Faroese landscape. Premiering at Fantasia, this is gothic romance at its most full-blooded with a love that refuses to stay buried.

Winner of the Palme dâOr and nominated for four Academy Awards, Scorseseâs raw portrait of urban alienation remains an essential diagnosis of a society defined by loneliness. Upon realizing the rumors were entirely fabricated and that he has ruined her reputation, a guilt-ridden Chuan signs up for Man's lessons under his real identity to make amends.


As they connect beyond the digital noise, a genuine romance blossoms. To clear her name, Chuan devises a plan to expose the disgruntled student who started the smear campaign, while encouraging Man to reclaim her professional standing by challenging celebrity coach Joe (Kevin Chu).

details.name: Bring Him Down to a Portable Size
details.title: Bring Him Down to a Portable Size
details.description:
Writer Riko receives a call from the police that her older brother has died unexpectedly. As she travels to where his brother had been living, painful memories of their troubled relationship begin to resurface.

 

Riko reunites for the first time in seven years with her brother's ex-wife, Kanako, his daughter Marina, and son Ryoichi, who is now in temporary child welfare care. As they clean out the garbage-filled apartment where his brother once lived, old photographs and forgotten belongings reveal unexpected truths about the man they thought they knew. Over four emotional days, the four confront grief, resentment, and long-buried memories, ultimately rediscovering what it means to be a family.

details.name: Farewell to my Concubine (4K Restored Version)
details.title: Farewell to my Concubine (4K Restored Version)
details.description:
Douzi, a boy with feminine features, is abandoned by his prostitute mother to an all-boys Peking opera troupe supervised by Master Guan. Douzi befriends fellow trouper Shitou.

A few years later in 1938, a teenage Douzi is trained to play dan (female roles), while Shitou learns jing (painted face male roles). When practicing the play "Dreaming of the World Outside the Nunnery", Douzi intentionally mistakes the line "I am by nature a girl, not a boy" with "I am by nature a boy, not a girl," subjecting himself to severe physical punishments. Douzi along with another student, Laizi, attempt to run away, but Douzi decides to pursue acting seriously after witnessing an opera performance. Upon returning, they find the whole troupe being punished for their desertion, and Douzi is beaten. As a result, Laizi hangs himself...

details.title: HEAT (4K Restoration)
details.description:
Heat is a gripping crime thriller directed by Michael Mann, starring Academy AwardÂ® winners Al Pacino and Robert De Niro. Neil McCauley (Robert De Niro), a highly skilled and disciplined professional thief who leads a crew specializing in high-stakes heists across Los Angeles. On the other side is Vincent Hanna (Al Pacino), a relentless LAPD detective whose dedication to his job matches McCauleyâs commitment to his criminal craft.

As McCauley and his crew plan their biggest score yet, Hanna and his team close in, leading to an intense game of cat and mouse. Both men struggle to balance their personal lives with their professional obsessions, blurring the lines between hunter and hunted. The film builds to a climactic confrontation, exploring themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the thin line separating lawmen from lawbreakers.

Renowned for its realistic action sequences, complex characters, and the legendary face-off between Pacino and De Niro, Heat is considered a landmark in the crime genre.
